title: Axiomarium eval case
description: An asset's evals/behavioral/<case>/eval.yaml or evals/regression/<case>/eval.yaml: a prompt that axm eval runs in a copy of the case's repo/ with the asset installed, and the checks that decide each run.

prompt.description: What the user asks, as they'd type it. It's the session's first message.

allow.description: Commands the session may run, each the start of a command line, such as axm validate. Claude Code denies every other command. Codex's sandbox can't hold a session to them, so a ran check reports the rest.

items.description: A command's leading words, such as axm validate, without parentheses or wildcards: axm writes each harness's own rule from them.

checks.description: What decides a run: it passes when every check passes. Each check is one of file, run, loaded, ran or reply.

judge.description: A rubric a model grades each run against. Its verdict is shown as model judgment and never changes what the checks decided.

rubric.description: What a good run does, in plain words.

guards.description: Regression cases only, and required for them: the failure this case guards against, and where it's recorded.

file.description: A glob relative to the repo, such as hooks/*/hook.md. Passes when a file matches it, or with contains, when a matching file contains the text. The repo's .git never matches.

contains.description: With file only: text a matching file must contain, in any case.

run.description: A command run in the repo after the session, where axm is the axm that runs the eval. Passes when it exits with exit.

exit.description: With run only: the exit code to expect. 0 when left out.

loaded.description: A skill the session loaded or an agent it ran, by name.

ran.description: The leading words of a command the session ran, such as git push. Each step of a chained command counts, by its program's name.

reply.description: Text the session's final message contains, in any case.

not.description: Passes when the check would fail, such as a file that must not exist. A run check says what to expect with exit instead.
